q: A game show has three doors, one with a car. I pick door 1. The host does not know where the car is. He opens door 3 at random, and it happens to show a goat. Should I switch to door 2?
why: it says switching helps (that is the host who knows)
reply:
From my own knowledge: This is the classic Monty Hall problem. The probability of winning by switching is 2/3, while staying is 1/3. The host's action of opening a door with a goat (which he knows is not the car) provides information that shifts the probability from the unchosen door to the remaining unopened door.

ANSWER: Yes, you should switch to door 2.

q: Write a Structured Text PLC program for a tank: open the fill valve when the low float switch comes on, and close it when the high float switch comes on.
why: the valve is not held open between the two floats
reply:
MAKE CODE: Tank Fill/Stop Logic
(* Structured Text PLC program for tank fill/stop logic *)
PROGRAM TankFillStop
VAR
    LowFloat AT %IX0.0 : BOOL;    (* Input: Low float switch *)
    HighFloat AT %IX0.1 : BOOL;   (* Input: High float switch *)
    FillValve AT %QX0.0 : BOOL;   (* Output: Fill valve *)
END_VAR
(* Open fill valve when low float is ON *)
FillValve := LowFloat;
END_PROGRAM
END
LESSON: Tank fill/stop logic
